title: Plant Tissues, Organs and Systems
seo_title: Biology 2: Plant Tissues, Organs and Systems Worksheets (Strengthened SHS)
standard_code: Biology 2, Quarter 3: Plant and Animal Tissues
standard_text: Plant cells, tissues (meristematic, dermal, ground, vascular), organs (roots, stems, leaves) and organ systems (root and shoot systems); transport, photosynthesis in leaves and plant growth. (summary of the Strengthened Senior High School curriculum, Biology 2, Quarter 3)
meta_desc: Free Biology 2 worksheets (Strengthened SHS curriculum, Quarter 3): plant tissues, roots, stems and leaves, transport in plants, photosynthesis in leaves and plant growth and hormones. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Xylem carries water up; phloem carries sugars to where they are used.
key_sub: Leaves are built for photosynthesis; stomata control gas exchange and water loss.
body_html:
How to think about it

Plants have three tissue systems: dermal (epidermis, guard cells, root hairs), ground (parenchyma, collenchyma, sclerenchyma) and vascular (xylem and phloem). Meristems at root and shoot tips make new cells for growth.

Water enters root hairs by osmosis and is pulled up the xylem by transpiration from the leaves. Sugars made in photosynthesis move in the phloem from sources (leaves) to sinks (roots, fruits). Hormones such as auxin, gibberellin and abscisic acid control growth and responses like phototropism.

Example

On a hot, windy day, what happens to the rate of transpiration?

More evaporation from the leaves

Answer: it increases

Example

Which hormone makes a shoot bend towards light?

Cells on the shaded side grow longer.

Answer: auxin

Common mistakes

  • Saying xylem carries sugars: xylem carries water and minerals.
  • Thinking plants take in food from the soil: they make sugars by photosynthesis.
  • Forgetting that stomata close to save water, which also slows photosynthesis.

items.q: Which tissue or structure is described as the innermost layer of the cortex, with Casparian strips in roots?
items.e: Endodermis: the innermost layer of the cortex, with Casparian strips in roots.

items.q: What is the outermost layer of the primary plant body?
items.e: It is covered by cuticle in shoots.

items.q: Which elements of xylem are found mainly in angiosperms?
items.e: Gymnosperms lack vessels.

items.q: Which description fits cuticle?
c: the layers just below the epidermis, of collenchyma in dicot stems
living cells thickened at the corners with cellulose and pectin
tall, closely packed cells with many chloroplasts below the upper epidermis
a waxy layer on the epidermis that cuts water loss
items.e: Cuticle: a waxy layer on the epidermis that cuts water loss.

items.q: Which description fits endodermis?
c: the innermost layer of the cortex, with Casparian strips in roots
large empty cells in grass leaves that make them roll up in dry weather
loosely arranged cells with air spaces in the lower part of a dicot leaf
items.e: Endodermis: the innermost layer of the cortex, with Casparian strips in roots.

items.q: Which feature is typical of a pancreatic cell that secretes enzymes?
c: no nucleus and a biconcave shape
a lot of rough endoplasmic reticulum and a large Golgi body
items.e: A pancreatic cell that secretes enzymes has a lot of rough endoplasmic reticulum and a large Golgi body: many proteins made and packaged for secretion.

items.q: What is a dorsiventral leaf?
c: a leaf with the same tissue on both sides
a leaf with palisade on the upper side and spongy tissue below, as in dicots
items.e: Isobilateral leaves (grasses) differ.

items.q: Which cell has no cytoplasm or cross-walls and lignified walls, giving an empty, continuous tube that carries water and gives support?
c: a pancreatic cell that secretes enzymes
items.e: Each specialized cell is adapted to its job.

items.q: Which cell has a tail (flagellum) and many mitochondria, giving energy to swim to the egg?
items.e: Each specialized cell is adapted to its job.

items.q: Which description fits phellogen?
c: the innermost layer of the cortex, with Casparian strips in roots
living cells thickened at the corners with cellulose and pectin
the cork cambium that makes cork and secondary cortex
the layers just below the epidermis, of collenchyma in dicot stems
items.e: Phellogen: the cork cambium that makes cork and secondary cortex.

items.q: Which tissue or structure is described as large empty cells in grass leaves that make them roll up in dry weather?
items.e: Bulliform cells: large empty cells in grass leaves that make them roll up in dry weather.

items.q: Which layer in the root has Casparian strips?
items.e: Suberin blocks water from moving through the walls.

items.q: Which feature is typical of a muscle cell?
c: no nucleus and a biconcave shape
no cytoplasm or cross-walls and lignified walls
items.e: A muscle cell has many mitochondria: more energy released by respiration for contraction.

items.q: Which description fits bulliform cells?
c: parenchyma cells between the vascular bundles of a dicot stem
cork, the dead outer layer of bark
large empty cells in grass leaves that make them roll up in dry weather
items.e: Bulliform cells: large empty cells in grass leaves that make them roll up in dry weather.

items.q: Which cells guard the stomata of grasses?
items.e: Dicots have bean-shaped guard cells.

items.q: Which cell has no nucleus and a biconcave shape, giving more room for hemoglobin and a larger surface area to take up oxygen?
c: a pancreatic cell that secretes enzymes
items.e: Each specialized cell is adapted to its job.

items.q: A sperm cell has a tail (flagellum) and many mitochondria. How does this help it?
c: a change of shape that opens and closes the stoma
a larger surface area to absorb water and mineral salts
energy to swim to the egg
many proteins made and packaged for secretion
items.e: Structure fits function.

items.q: A xylem vessel has no cytoplasm or cross-walls and lignified walls. How does this help it?
c: an empty, continuous tube that carries water and gives support
a larger surface area to absorb water and mineral salts
a change of shape that opens and closes the stoma
energy to swim to the egg
items.e: Structure fits function.

items.q: Which description fits lenticels?
c: tall, closely packed cells with many chloroplasts below the upper epidermis
openings in the bark for gas exchange
a waxy layer on the epidermis that cuts water loss
the innermost layer of the cortex, with Casparian strips in roots
items.e: Lenticels: openings in the bark for gas exchange.

items.q: A guard cell has a thicker inner wall. How does this help it?
c: many proteins made and packaged for secretion
energy to swim to the egg
a change of shape that opens and closes the stoma
items.e: Structure fits function.

items.q: Which description fits phloem?
c: openings in the bark for gas exchange
living cells thickened at the corners with cellulose and pectin
tall, closely packed cells with many chloroplasts below the upper epidermis
items.e: Phloem: transporting food from leaves.

items.q: In which organ is this seen: vascular bundles in a ring, conjoint, open, with cambium?
items.e: Dicot stem: vascular bundles in a ring, conjoint, open, with cambium.

items.q: Which tissue or structure is described as loosely arranged cells with air spaces in the lower part of a dicot leaf?
items.e: Spongy parenchyma: loosely arranged cells with air spaces in the lower part of a dicot leaf.

items.q: In which organ is this seen: scattered vascular bundles, conjoint and closed, with a bundle sheath?
items.e: Monocot stem: scattered vascular bundles, conjoint and closed, with a bundle sheath.

items.q: What does the vascular cambium produce?
c: secondary xylem on the inside and secondary phloem on the outside
items.e: This causes growth in girth.

items.q: Which description fits a dicot root?
c: vascular bundles in a ring, conjoint, open, with cambium
scattered vascular bundles, conjoint and closed, with a bundle sheath
radial vascular bundles, 2–4 xylem bundles and a small pith
radial vascular bundles, more than six xylem bundles and a large pith
items.e: Dicot root: radial vascular bundles, 2–4 xylem bundles and a small pith.

items.q: Which description fits a dicot stem?
c: vascular bundles in a ring, conjoint, open, with cambium
radial vascular bundles, 2–4 xylem bundles and a small pith
scattered vascular bundles, conjoint and closed, with a bundle sheath
radial vascular bundles, more than six xylem bundles and a large pith
items.e: Dicot stem: vascular bundles in a ring, conjoint, open, with cambium.

items.q: What is a racemose inflorescence?
c: one in which the main axis keeps growing and flowers form laterally
items.e: Flowers open from the base upward.

items.q: Which plants have no secondary growth usually?
items.e: They lack a vascular cambium.

items.q: Which description fits a monocot stem?
c: radial vascular bundles, 2–4 xylem bundles and a small pith
vascular bundles in a ring, conjoint, open, with cambium
scattered vascular bundles, conjoint and closed, with a bundle sheath
radial vascular bundles, more than six xylem bundles and a large pith
items.e: Monocot stem: scattered vascular bundles, conjoint and closed, with a bundle sheath.

items.q: Which description fits spongy parenchyma?
c: cork, the dead outer layer of bark
loosely arranged cells with air spaces in the lower part of a dicot leaf
living cells thickened at the corners with cellulose and pectin
specialized parenchyma cells linked to sieve tubes
items.e: Spongy parenchyma: loosely arranged cells with air spaces in the lower part of a dicot leaf.

items.q: What is an epigynous flower?
c: one in which the ovary is inferior
one in which the ovary is superior
items.e: e.g. guava, cucumber and sunflower ray florets.

items.q: Which tissue or structure is described as specialized parenchyma cells linked to sieve tubes?
items.e: Companion cells: specialized parenchyma cells linked to sieve tubes.

items.q: Which tissue or structure is described as the cork cambium that makes cork and secondary cortex?
items.e: Phellogen: the cork cambium that makes cork and secondary cortex.

items.q: Which part of phloem is absent in gymnosperms?
items.e: They have albuminous cells and sieve cells.

items.q: Which root system do dicots usually have?
items.e: The primary root goes on growing.

items.q: What are stamens attached to petals called?
items.e: e.g. brinjal.

items.q: What is the cotyledon of a grass seed called?
items.e: It is a single large shield-shaped cotyledon.

items.q: Which tissue or structure is described as a waxy layer on the epidermis that cuts water loss?
items.e: Cuticle: a waxy layer on the epidermis that cuts water loss.

items.q: Which is a parthenocarpic fruit?
items.e: It develops without fertilization.

items.q: What is the cohesion–tension theory?
c: water evaporating from leaves pulls a continuous column of water up the xylem
root pressure pushes all water up
items.e: Hydrogen bonds hold the water molecules together.

items.q: Why do stomata close at night in most plants?
c: there is no light for photosynthesis, so closing reduces water loss
items.e: Guard cells lose turgor.

items.q: What is the effect of drier air on the rate of transpiration?
items.e: Transpiration is faster when the air is warm, dry and moving and the stomata are open in light.

items.q: In a potometer, the air bubble moves 15 cm along the tube in 4 minutes. What is the rate of water uptake in cm per minute?
items.e: Rate = distance ÷ time = 15 ÷ 4.

items.q: What are companion cells for?
c: providing ATP for active loading of sucrose into sieve tubes
items.e: They have many mitochondria.

items.q: What is the effect of lower temperature on the rate of transpiration?
items.e: Transpiration is faster when the air is warm, dry and moving and the stomata are open in light.

items.q: In a potometer, the air bubble moves 5 cm along the tube in 4 minutes. What is the rate of water uptake in cm per minute?
items.e: Rate = distance ÷ time = 5 ÷ 4.

items.q: In 5 minutes an air bubble in a potometer moves 36 mm along a capillary tube of radius 0.60 mm. Calculate the rate of water uptake in mm³ min⁻¹.
items.e: Volume = πr²d = π × 0.60² × 36 = 40.7 mm³; ÷ 5 min = 8.14 mm³ min⁻¹.

items.q: In 2 minutes an air bubble in a potometer moves 18 mm along a capillary tube of radius 0.25 mm. Calculate the rate of water uptake in mm³ min⁻¹.
items.e: Volume = πr²d = π × 0.25² × 18 = 3.53 mm³; ÷ 2 min = 1.77 mm³ min⁻¹.

items.q: How do radioactive tracers show translocation?
c: dye shows water in the xylem
¹⁴CO₂ is supplied to a leaf and labeled sugars are found in the phloem
items.e: Autoradiography shows the path.

items.q: What is the effect of higher humidity on the rate of transpiration?
items.e: Transpiration is faster when the air is warm, dry and moving and the stomata are open in light.

items.q: What does phloem transport?
items.e: This is translocation.

items.q: What is the effect of windy conditions on the rate of transpiration?
items.e: Transpiration is faster when the air is warm, dry and moving and the stomata are open in light.

items.q: Which factor increases the rate of transpiration?
items.e: Molecules evaporate faster.

items.q: In a potometer, the air bubble moves 3 cm along the tube in 2 minutes. What is the rate of water uptake in cm per minute?
items.e: Rate = distance ÷ time = 3 ÷ 2.

items.q: In 6 minutes an air bubble in a potometer moves 25 mm along a capillary tube of radius 1.0 mm. Calculate the rate of water uptake in mm³ min⁻¹.
items.e: Volume = πr²d = π × 1.0² × 25 = 78.5 mm³; ÷ 6 min = 13.1 mm³ min⁻¹.

items.q: In 10 minutes an air bubble in a potometer moves 18 mm along a capillary tube of radius 1.0 mm. Calculate the rate of water uptake in mm³ min⁻¹.
items.e: Volume = πr²d = π × 1.0² × 18 = 56.5 mm³; ÷ 10 min = 5.65 mm³ min⁻¹.

items.q: What is the mass flow hypothesis?
c: sucrose loaded at the source lowers water potential, water enters and pressure pushes the sap to the sink
items.e: Sinks include roots and growing tips.

items.q: In a potometer, the air bubble moves 8 cm along the tube in 2 minutes. What is the rate of water uptake in cm per minute?
items.e: Rate = distance ÷ time = 8 ÷ 2.

items.q: In 6 minutes an air bubble in a potometer moves 45 mm along a capillary tube of radius 1.0 mm. Calculate the rate of water uptake in mm³ min⁻¹.
items.e: Volume = πr²d = π × 1.0² × 45 = 141 mm³; ÷ 6 min = 23.6 mm³ min⁻¹.

items.q: A water plant gives off 45 bubbles of oxygen in 3 minutes. What is the rate of photosynthesis in bubbles per minute?
items.e: Rate = 45 ÷ 3. Counting bubbles measures the oxygen released.

items.q: A water plant gives off 40 bubbles of oxygen in 4 minutes. What is the rate of photosynthesis in bubbles per minute?
items.e: Rate = 40 ÷ 4. Counting bubbles measures the oxygen released.

items.q: A greenhouse plant has lots of light and water, but the air has little CO<sub>2</sub>. What limits photosynthesis?
items.e: The factor in shortest supply limits the rate.

items.q: A water plant gives off 18 bubbles of oxygen in 2 minutes. What is the rate of photosynthesis in bubbles per minute?
items.e: Rate = 18 ÷ 2. Counting bubbles measures the oxygen released.

items.q: A plant on a shady forest floor has plenty of water and CO<sub>2</sub>. What limits its photosynthesis?
items.e: The factor in shortest supply limits the rate.

items.q: A water plant gives off 15 bubbles of oxygen in 5 minutes. What is the rate of photosynthesis in bubbles per minute?
items.e: Rate = 15 ÷ 5. Counting bubbles measures the oxygen released.

items.q: Leaves at the top of a tree get more light. Compared with shaded leaves, what do they usually do?
items.e: The factor in shortest supply limits the rate.

items.q: Which chemical is used for killing broad-leaved weeds?
items.e: 2,4-D: killing broad-leaved weeds.

items.q: What is the arithmetic growth equation?
items.e: Only one daughter cell keeps dividing.

items.q: Which effect is caused by gibberellin?
c: closing stomata and seed dormancy (the stress hormone)
stem elongation and bolting in cabbage
cell division and delaying leaf senescence
items.e: Gibberellin: stem elongation and bolting in cabbage.

items.q: Which hormone was first isolated from human urine?
items.e: Auxin means 'to grow'.

items.q: What is photoperiodism?
c: the response of plants to the relative lengths of day and night
items.e: It controls flowering.

items.q: Which hormone is a gas?
items.e: It speeds ripening.

items.q: Which hormone was discovered from the 'bakanae' disease of rice?
items.e: Gibberella fujikuroi caused tall seedlings.

items.q: Where is the stimulus for photoperiodic flowering perceived?
items.e: A hormone then moves to the shoot tip.

items.q: Which effect is caused by ethene?
c: cell division and delaying leaf senescence
apical dominance and root initiation on stem cuttings
stem elongation and bolting in cabbage
items.e: Ethylene: fruit ripening and leaf fall.

items.q: What is ethephon used for in agriculture?
c: hastening fruit ripening and flowering in pineapple
increasing the length of grape stalks and sugarcane stems
items.e: Ethephon: hastening fruit ripening and flowering in pineapple.

items.q: What is GA₃ used for in agriculture?
c: hastening fruit ripening and flowering in pineapple
increasing the length of grape stalks and sugarcane stems
items.e: GA₃: increasing the length of grape stalks and sugarcane stems.

items.q: What is 2,4-D used for in agriculture?
c: increasing the length of grape stalks and sugarcane stems
hastening fruit ripening and flowering in pineapple
items.e: 2,4-D: killing broad-leaved weeds.

items.q: Which hormone is found in coconut milk and maize kernels?
items.e: Kinetin was first found in autoclaved herring sperm DNA.

items.q: Which effect is caused by auxin?
c: cell division and delaying leaf senescence
apical dominance and root initiation on stem cuttings
stem elongation and bolting in cabbage
items.e: Auxin: apical dominance and root initiation on stem cuttings.

items.q: Which plant hormone causes apical dominance and root initiation on stem cuttings?
items.e: Auxin: apical dominance and root initiation on stem cuttings.

items.q: Which chemical is used for hastening fruit ripening and flowering in pineapple?
items.e: Ethephon: hastening fruit ripening and flowering in pineapple.

items.q: Which hormone is called the stress hormone?
items.e: It helps plants survive drought.

items.q: Which chemical is used for rooting of stem cuttings?
items.e: NAA: rooting of stem cuttings.

items.q: What is NAA used for in agriculture?
c: increasing the length of grape stalks and sugarcane stems
hastening fruit ripening and flowering in pineapple
items.e: NAA: rooting of stem cuttings.

items.q: Which plant hormone causes cell division and delaying leaf senescence?
items.e: Cytokinin: cell division and delaying leaf senescence.
